notes: Racing rather than Survival: a runaway train sounds like a disaster prompt, but Disaster Survival's win is outlasting the timer in a bounded arena, while here the timer running out is the loss and the player chases down a moving target along a line at speed — forward translation on a designated route from a start point to an end point. route-point-to-point is the genre default and matches the space exactly: the line begins behind the runaway and terminates at the sharp curve over the river, three towns later. Obstacle Race is the closest preset for a one-way course with things in the way, so hazard-kill carries both the trackside obstacles and the river gorge that punishes leaving the rails, trigger-finish is the terminal detection zone at the curve, and the answers' three small industrial railroad towns are settlement-density; I dropped the preset's checkpoint-respawn because a single ten-minute attempt ending in derailment restarts the round rather than restoring mid-course. Racing's genre-wide P6 is kept and is the right build here, since a rail line through three towns has to read as one continuous unambiguous route; the river is a barrier under the curve rather than a swimmable volume, so water-body's CHECK clears, and the smashable trackside objects have no option in the loaded table — they are a dressing request on top of hazard-kill.
